# Affine frusta: bounded cone laws and exact truncation compensation

This note proves an exact reduction of slope records for an affine frustum. It does not prove the remaining sharp comparison. The physical measure is retained throughout.

Let d=m+1>=2, H>0, B=H+1, and 0<U<H. Set

    r(z)=(H-z)/B,   -1<=z<=U,
    a=r(U),        T=U/a=H/a-B>0,
    t=a^d,         V0=B/d,        V=(1-t)V0,
    C0=(H/B)^m,    p0=(H/B)^d,   a0=1/B.

The planar density is r(z)^(m-1)/2 on |x|<=r(z). A slope law becomes an even unimodal base law phi, a mixture of uniforms [-s,s], exactly as in `candidate 6146c77d1d7c5e08`.

## 1. Two-sided truncated energy records

The partial rays are precisely -T<b<1. With

    v=phi{b<=1},    w=phi{b>=-T},
    e(q)=int_[-T,1](1-qb)^(-d)dphi(b),

direct ray integration gives

    P/V0=p0 e(a0)+(1-v)-t w,
    C/C0=e(a0),
    M/C0=-(H/B)int_[-T,1]b(1-b/B)^(-d-1)dphi(b).       (1)

To check the cap constant, fully captured rays b>=1 contribute 1-t, partial rays contribute [H/(B-b)]^d-t, and rays b<=-T contribute zero. Thus the subtraction t applies to EVERY ray with b>-T, including fully captured ones. Writing only -t times the partial-ray probability would omit the corresponding part of the full-ray subtraction.

As before, M=0 is exactly e'(a0)=0 for the FIXED interval [-T,1]. Its positive denominator is bounded below on that interval. This gives an attained scalar convex-energy minimum, but the one-sided energy bounds alone do not prove the frustum inequality after the negative term -t w is retained.

## 2. A complete one-sign branch

If T<=1, every finite positive uniform layer has strictly positive

    int_[-T,1]b(1-a0 b)^(-d-1)dphi_s(b).

Indeed its symmetric part around zero contributes a positive value by pairing b and -b, and its unmatched part, if any, is on the positive side. Therefore M(s)<0 for every finite s>0. A centered probability law of finite slopes must be concentrated at zero. If the slope line is compactified, it may also use infinity, whose record is (V/2,0,0). For such centered laws one common correction c=(P(0)-V/2)/C(0) makes P-cC exactly V/2. Every balanced two-law expression is consequently 1/2 when its denominator is positive.

This case needs no multiplier attainment or approximation.

## 3. The nontrivial branch reduces exactly to bounded cone slopes

Assume T>=1. For every slope 0<=s<=T, all rays removed by truncating the cone above z=U are captured: their least margin occurs at z=U,b=-s and equals U-as>=0. Therefore the full-cone and frustum records satisfy

    P_frustum(s)=P_cone(s)-t V0,
    C_frustum(s)=C_cone(s),
    M_frustum(s)=M_cone(s).                         (2)

Equality at the cutoff s=T is harmless because its exceptional base ray has zero uniform-layer mass.

For s>=T, both physical axial endpoints lie in the section strip: the left endpoint condition is s>=1 and the right one is s>=T. Hence the direct formulas are

    C(s)=(1/(2s))int_-1^U r(z)^(m-1)dz,
    M(s)=(1/(2s))int_-1^U z r(z)^(m-1)dz,
    P(s)=V/2+M(s).                                (3)

In particular the entire record at s is the convex combination

    record(s)=(T/s) record(T)+(1-T/s)(V/2,0,0).     (4)

Thus ANY frustum slope law can be replaced, with all three records unchanged, by a law supported on [0,T] plus an atom at infinity. Its finite part is separately centered whenever the original law is centered, because the infinity record has zero moment. By (2), that finite part is also a centered law for the original full cone.

For T<1 the full-section formula begins only at s>=1, not at s=T; Section 2 handled that branch independently. No incorrect tail replacement across that intermediate region is used.

## 4. Exact compensation in the two-law target

First consider two normalized centered laws mu,nu supported on [0,T]. Let P_mu,P_nu,C_mu,C_nu denote their FULL-CONE records. Their frustum balanced expression is exactly

    beta_frustum=(beta_cone-t omega)/(1-t),
    beta_cone=[C_nu P_mu+C_mu(V0-P_nu)]/[V0(C_mu+C_nu)],
    omega=C_nu/(C_mu+C_nu).                        (5)

The correction is directional: it is t times omega, not a symmetric loss t/2. Therefore the proved cone bound beta_cone>=4/9 cannot simply be divided by 1-t to settle the frustum.

For laws with infinity atoms, the corresponding additional records are (V/2,0,0), and (4) keeps them exactly. A uniform common-c inequality for all centered finite laws supported on [0,T] would automatically include these atoms, since their corrected value is V/2. The unresolved numerical obligation in this route is precisely a bound on the loss t omega in (5), using the bounded support of the centered cone laws and the relation t=[H/(B+T)]^d.

One valid but generally insufficient energy refinement follows from bounded support. For a centered cone law supported on [0,T], its base law is supported on [-T,T]. With v=phi{b<=1} and e=int_(b<=1)(1-b/B)^(-d)dphi,

    e >= (2v-1)+[t/p0](1-v).                      (6)

The symmetric part [-1,1] pays 2v-1 by Jensen; the remaining negative tail has mass 1-v and denominator factor at least (1+T/B)^(-d)=t/p0. This retains some of the truncation cost but is not asserted sufficient for the exact Gamma_d inequality.
